q: If the environment does not change, then natural selection maintains populations or organisms so they do not change much over ____.
e: If the environment does not change, then natural selection maintains populations or organisms so they do not change much over time. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Natural selection will bring about a change to a species over time. Thus selection of adaptive variation is the mechanism by which ____ occurs.
e: Natural selection will bring about a change to a species over time. Thus selection of adaptive variation is the mechanism by which evolution occurs. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Being adapted means being specialized to suit the environment in which organism ____.
e: Being adapted means being specialized to suit the environment in which organism lives. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Features which enable organisms to survive are called ____.
e: Features which enable organisms to survive are called adaptations. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological or ____.
e: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological or behavioural. Behavioural adaptations are things an animal does, such as seeking shade. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water.

q: Anatomical adaptations are the structures of an organism that is modified to perform an adapted ____.
e: Anatomical adaptations are the structures of an organism that is modified to perform an adapted function. Function is what a structure does in the living body. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Physiological adaptations are features of the processes inside an organism's body that increase its chance of survival or ____.
e: Physiological adaptations are features of the processes inside an organism's body that increase its chance of survival or reproduction. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Behavioural adaptations are any actions by organisms which help them to survive or ____.
e: Behavioural adaptations are any actions by organisms which help them to survive or reproduce. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. Behavioural adaptations are things an animal does, such as seeking shade.

q: Camels live and breed in desert, which is hottest, driest and most challenging ____.
e: Camels live and breed in desert, which is hottest, driest and most challenging environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Presence of closable nostrils and long eyelashes help keep out wind-blown ____.
e: Presence of closable nostrils and long eyelashes help keep out wind-blown sand. Sand is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Having large and flat feet with tough pads allows to spread out the weight of the camel as it walks over ____.
e: Having large and flat feet with tough pads allows to spread out the weight of the camel as it walks over sand. Sand is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The fatty tissue in the hump acts as food ____.
e: The fatty tissue in the hump acts as food store. Store is the biological term this statement needs.

q: As the fat is broken down to release energy during cellular respiration, water is produced as a ____.
e: As the fat is broken down to release energy during cellular respiration, water is produced as a by-product. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Viruses are not cellular.

q: The kidneys minimize the production of ____.
e: The kidneys minimize the production of urine. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions.

q: They sit down early in the morning before the ground warms up with their legs tucked underneath, so they can absorb a little heat from the ____.
e: They sit down early in the morning before the ground warms up with their legs tucked underneath, so they can absorb a little heat from the ground. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Groups of camels may lie down together, so that minimizing the amount of surface of each camel exposed to ____.
e: Groups of camels may lie down together, so that minimizing the amount of surface of each camel exposed to sun. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: As they are browsers, they can eat a wide range of vegetation in desert, where carnivorous habit is ____.
e: As they are browsers, they can eat a wide range of vegetation in desert, where carnivorous habit is impossible. Impossible is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection is the process by which organisms that are well adapted to their environment have a greater chance to breed and pass on their alleles to the next ____.
e: Natural selection is the process by which organisms that are well adapted to their environment have a greater chance to breed and pass on their alleles to the next generation. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Forms that are not well adapted will not ____.
e: Forms that are not well adapted will not survive. Survive is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Beneficial mutations are the 'raw material' that are ultimately the source of new inherited ____.
e: Beneficial mutations are the 'raw material' that are ultimately the source of new inherited variation. Variation is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is the breeding of only those individuals with desired features as human choice, rather than environmental ____.
e: Artificial selection is the breeding of only those individuals with desired features as human choice, rather than environmental factors. Factors is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is also called ____.
e: Artificial selection is also called selective breeding. Selective breeding is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Farmers have bred crop plants of all kinds to obtain increased ____.
e: Farmers have bred crop plants of all kinds to obtain increased yield. Yield is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They selectively bred one species of wild brassica (Brassica oleracea) to give several strains, each with specific ____.
e: They selectively bred one species of wild brassica (Brassica oleracea) to give several strains, each with specific features. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Modern selective breeding methods are cloning plants such as micropropagation and cloning animals by ____.
e: Modern selective breeding methods are cloning plants such as micropropagation and cloning animals by genetic modification. Modern biotechnology can move genes even between unrelated species.

q: Natural selection produces greater ____.
e: Natural selection produces greater biodiversity. Biodiversity is the variety of species, genes, and ecosystems.

q: Artificial selection produces varieties of organisms very different from native ____.
e: Artificial selection produces varieties of organisms very different from native generations. Generations is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection may lead to new ____.
e: Natural selection may lead to new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Artificial selection does not result in new ____.
e: Artificial selection does not result in new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: In natural selection, outbreeding is common, leading to hybrid ____.
e: In natural selection, outbreeding is common, leading to hybrid vigour. Vigour is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common, leading to loss of vigour in the ____.
e: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common, leading to loss of vigour in the offspring. Offspring is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection is a slow process, taking many ____.
e: Natural selection is a slow process, taking many years. Years is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is a relatively ____ process.
e: Artificial selection is a relatively fast process. Fast is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In natural selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population remains ____.
e: In natural selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population remains high. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area.

q: In artificial selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population is ____.
e: In artificial selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population is reduced. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area.
